risks.description: The approve call may apply the payment/approval effect and then stall past any sane client timeout, so the caller receives no definitive response and cannot tell whether the invoice was approved. The effect is real but the outcome is ambiguous to the client.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (approving records the approval durably) — an approval that lands but is never confirmed to the caller undermines the durable-record guarantee's usefulness.

risks.description: Two approvals of the same invoice arriving simultaneously may each apply the effect, double-recording the approval and double-paying, if the endpoint checks-then-sets without proper serialization.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 — a durable approval record that counts the same approval twice is not a faithful record.

risks.description: An earlier invoice's persisted approval may not survive an independent re-read after a subsequent write to the store (clobbered / not truly durable), violating the survives-a-re-read guarantee.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 (approval state survives a re-read of persisted state).

risks.description: An approve request with no actor field may fail to record the approval durably or crash, dropping a legitimate approval.
A malformed request body may either crash the endpoint (5xx) or, worse, persist a spurious approval that no valid actor requested.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 — the durable store must reflect only genuine approvals.

scenarios.title: Approve that stalls past the client timeout still resolves to a definitive, single durable effect
scenarios.purpose: Detect the ambiguous-outcome defect where the approval effect lands but the response stalls past a sane client timeout, leaving the caller unable to tell what happened. This is the one covered gap: idempotency and persistence are exercised, timeout-after-effect is not.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a dedicated invoice id (UNIT-APPROVAL-TO-1) touched by no other scenario; the fixture reseeds the store on each service boot, so no residue crosses scenarios.
expected_observations: POST /approve returns a definitive response within the 4s client timeout
The durable store shows the invoice approved with exactly one payment
forbidden_observations: The approve request exceeds the client timeout with no response, leaving the outcome ambiguous
The durable store disagrees with what the HTTP response implied

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of the same invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race the sequential idempotency test cannot: concurrent approvals that could each pass a check-then-set and double-record/double-pay. Verifies serialization holds under contention.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id UNIT-APPROVAL-RACE-1; fixture reseeds store on boot.
expected_observations: Durable store records exactly one approval and one payment despite two concurrent approve calls
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows two payments or two approvals from the concurrent calls

scenarios.title: An approval survives an independent re-read after a later write to the store
scenarios.purpose: Verify AC-APPROVAL-002 specifically: an earlier invoice's persisted approval must still be present on an independent durable re-read after a subsequent, unrelated approval writes the store. Guards against clobbering / in-memory-only persistence.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice ids UNIT-APPROVAL-A and UNIT-APPROVAL-B; fixture reseeds store on boot.
expected_observations: An independent re-read of the durable store shows invoice A still approved after invoice B was approved
forbidden_observations: Invoice A reads back as pending after B's write
Invoice A is missing from the durable store

scenarios.title: Approval with no actor is still recorded durably
scenarios.purpose: Confirm a legitimate approval missing the optional actor field is not silently dropped and is still persisted with a single payment.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id UNIT-APPROVAL-NOACTOR; fixture reseeds store on boot.
expected_observations: Durable store records the approval and a single payment even though no actor was supplied
forbidden_observations: Durable store still shows the invoice pending after a 200 response

scenarios.title: Malformed approve body must not persist a spurious approval
scenarios.purpose: Ensure a non-object/garbage request body neither crashes the endpoint nor writes a spurious approval that no valid actor requested. The durable record must reflect only genuine approvals.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id UNIT-APPROVAL-MALFORMED; fixture reseeds store on boot.
expected_observations: The endpoint rejects the malformed body with a 4xx and records no approval
The durable store shows no payment for the invoice
forbidden_observations: The endpoint returns a 5xx / crashes on a malformed body
A spurious approval or payment is persisted from a malformed request

unresolved_questions: AC-APPROVAL-002 says approval state must 'survive a re-read of persisted state'. Does this include surviving a full process restart? The current build reseeds/wipes the store on every service boot, so restart-survival cannot be verified against it and a restart_recovery scenario would fail even on correct behavior — clarify whether restart durability is in scope.

Should approving an unknown/never-seen invoice id return 404 or auto-create the invoice? The build auto-creates on first touch, but no acceptance criterion specifies this, so it cannot be verified as promised behavior.

Is any actor identity or authorization required to approve an invoice? No auth is present and none is promised in the ACs or principle ids shown, so authorization / cross_tenant scenarios cannot be grounded.

Is a defined error contract expected for malformed bodies (specific status/shape)? The malformed_input scenario assumes a 4xx rejection derived from AC-APPROVAL-001's 'only genuine approvals' intent; an explicit contract would firm this up.
